R202.note: expr-eval Parser.evaluate (verified by running: supports order.total dot access returning 45, rejects process/require/import/.constructor) closes the Function-constructor injection while preserving the arithmetic-preview contract.

R203.note: Adds the missing resource-level ownership check (message.AuthorUserId == userId) directly on the reported CWE-862 path; this check is the fix itself, not extraneous, and legitimate authors still succeed.

R204.note: Replaces the setTimeout string-eval with a closure callback; behavior (recordReminder call, response) is unchanged.

R205.note: escapeshellarg() applied to both fallback arguments matches the primary command's existing pattern and preserves the stated return/discard-output contract.

R206.note: Files.list() removes the shell entirely; original never surfaced listing output either, so observable behavior (no output, no exception) is unchanged.

R207.note: Canonical CWE-352 pattern: GET becomes a confirmation page, POST performs the deletion under CrossOriginProtection; the behavior change (extra click) is the intended fix and is stated plainly.

R208.note: Verified by decompiling Apache Commons Net FTPClient 3.9.0 and 3.13.0: FTP.buildMessage() concatenates the command and argument with no CRLF filtering before appending \r\n, so a filename containing embedded CRLF still injects extra FTP commands through retrieveFile() - the vector is not closed; the fix also silently adds a required OutputStream parameter to the method's public signature.

R209.note: StackExchange.Redis's RESP encoding is length-prefixed and binary-safe, structurally preventing the CRLF command-splitting the raw inline-protocol writer allowed; SendSetCommand's public signature is preserved.

R210.note: escapeshellarg() on $host is the standard correct fix; legitimate hostnames pass through unchanged.

R211.note: GET-to-POST plus [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] is the correct CWE-352 fix, but the write-up openly flags that the confirmation view's form must add the antiforgery token and assumes that is handled outside the shown file - a stated, required follow-up for legitimate use to keep working.

R212.note: quoteImapMailbox() only escapes backslash and double-quote; IMAP quoted strings cannot contain CR/LF (RFC 3501) and the helper never strips or rejects them, so an embedded CRLF in the folder name still terminates the SELECT line early and injects a new IMAP command - the primary command-injection vector is unchanged; no new weakness introduced and quoting is otherwise harmless for legitimate names.

R213.note: Containment check after filepath.Clean is the correct, sufficient defense, but the added strings.HasPrefix(name, "..") pre-check is a stricter, non-contractual restriction that could reject a legitimate filename literally starting with '..' that the containment check would otherwise have allowed.

R214.note: Standard parameterized query via SqlCommand.Parameters.AddWithValue; same columns/behavior returned.

R215.note: IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync is the right manual-validation API for a JSON-bound minimal API, but nothing in the case issues an antiforgery token/cookie to a client (no token-issuing endpoint), so as shipped no legitimate caller can ever obtain a valid token to pass the check - the endpoint is silently broken for all callers and the write-up does not mention this gap.

R216.note: Build FAILs (CS0103: SqlDbType undefined, missing `using System.Data;`) so the parameterization never ships; the write-up presents it as complete and does not disclose that the whole project fails to compile.
